holidays.name: National Carrot Cake Day
holidays.description: Today is for cream cheese frosting and the one dessert that sneaks vegetables into cake. Bake a spiced, walnut-studded loaf, or just grab a slice and call it a salad.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It has become a yearly fixture on dessert calendars.
holidays.funFact: Carrot cake probably dates to medieval Europe. Sugar was expensive then, and cooks sweetened desserts with carrots instead.

holidays.name: National Golden Retriever Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the fluffy, tennis-ball-obsessed dogs who treat every stranger as a long-lost best friend. Take a walk, buy a squeaky toy, or just give a golden a very good scratch behind the ears.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial pet observance of unclear origin. It was created by dog lovers to honor the breed's friendly nature.
holidays.funFact: Golden retrievers were bred in 19th-century Scotland to fetch waterfowl for hunters. That is why so many of them still carry things around and love water.

holidays.name: Feed the Birds Day
holidays.description: Today you scatter some seed and make friends with your local feathered neighbors. Fill a feeder, put out a little birdseed, and watch the free daily show.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is often linked to the tuppence-a-bag bird feeding song from the film Mary Poppins.
holidays.funFact: Many small songbirds, such as chickadees, can lose a surprising share of their body weight overnight in winter. That makes a morning snack important for them.
